-   Sorting particles: $O(n)$ with Radix Sort on CPU/GPU for all slices, or $O(m \log(n))$ for $m$ slices using parallel reduction [S1, unofficial].

The claim states that Radix Sort can be performed on 'CPU/GPU'. However, the evidence explicitly states: 'We use a Radix Sort in CUDA to sort the indices...'. CUDA is a GPU computing platform. The evidence further clarifies that the $O(n)$ complexity is achieved by sorting on the GPU and then using 'two loops on the CPU' to retrieve the indices. It does not support the claim that the Radix Sort itself is performed on the CPU; rather, the CPU performs the linear scan after the GPU sorting. The second part of the claim regarding $O(m log(n))$ for $m$ slices using parallel reduction is supported by the text. Because the claim incorrectly attributes the Radix Sort operation to the CPU (or implies it can be done on the CPU in the same context as the GPU version), the evidence does not fully support the claim.
